content.intro: Learn configuring a database through a compact visual, an inspectable Django example, and a practical verification task.
content.why_it_matters: Configuring a Database matters because a Django project has to behave predictably across requests, database state, configuration, and deployments. Understanding this piece makes the surrounding application easier to test, maintain, and secure.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This lesson examines configuring a database as part of database configuration, migrations, and transactions. The objective is to understand the behavior, connect it to the listed subtopics, and verify it with a small example rather than relying on memorized syntax.

content_blocks.title: What to cover
content_blocks.text: The source syllabus for this lesson names: The DATABASES setting; Database engine and credentials; Connection configuration; Local and remote databases; Keeping credentials out of source code. Keep these distinct concepts together: know what each item does, when it applies, and what assumption must be verified in your project.

content_blocks.title: Worked example: Configuring a Database
content_blocks.code:
from django.db.models import Count

# Example QuerySet; assumes Book has a category relation.
Book.objects.values("category__name").annotate(total=Count("id")).order_by("category__name")
content_blocks.expected_output: The QuerySet groups records by related category name and annotates a count.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Open a local project using the documented Django 6.1-compatible Python environment. If this snippet depends on model names, URL configuration, settings, or an optional package, add those prerequisites before running it. Otherwise inspect it as a static example. CodeLeaf browser preview does not execute Django/Python server code.

content_blocks.title: Common mistakes and fixes
content_blocks.text: Common pitfalls include skipping a required configuration/import, copying a fragment without its model or URL context, trusting client input, or treating a development-only behavior as production-ready. Check the earliest failing assumption, consult the version-specific docs, and add a regression test for the failure you found.
